_about: Hanzi Grid grammar notes. Each key is a Chinese Grammar Wiki point id (see index.json and SOURCE.md); entries with another key give their own 'url'. 'key' is the character or word the point is about, so the grid can show how well you know it. Explanations and example sentences were written for Hanzi Grid; the 'source' link is the wiki article the rule is taken from.

ASGPNV3Q.explain: 有 is negated with 没, never with 不.

ASGIPYFV.explain: 不 negates present and future actions, habits and adjectives. For something that did not happen, use 没 instead.
ASGIPYFV.note: 不 is read bú before a 4th tone: 不是 bú shì.

ASG9YK09.explain: 都 means "all" and refers back to what comes before it. It goes before the verb.
examples: Zhèxiē shū dōu shì wǒ de.

ASGG25MD.explain: 也 means "also". It goes before the verb, never at the end of the sentence.

ASGP0KFF.explain: 和 joins nouns and pronouns. It does not join two sentences the way English "and" does.
examples: Bàba hé māma dōu zài jiā.
Dad and mum are both at home.

ASGA8NIB.explain: 还是 offers a choice in a question: "A or B?". In statements, "or" is 或者.
examples: Is he a teacher or a student?
我们今天去还是明天去？
Wǒmen jīntiān qù háishi míngtiān qù?
Are we going today or tomorrow?

ASGQUKJF.explain: Age is stated with a number and 岁, without 是. Ask 几岁 for a child, 多大 for anyone.
examples: How old are you? (to a child)

ASGI0T9S.explain: Every counted noun needs a measure word. 个 is the general one and works for people and most things.

ASGT3KF6.pattern: year 年 + month 月 + day 号/日
ASGT3KF6.explain: Dates go from big to small: year, month, day. 号 is spoken, 日 is written.
examples: Jīntiān shì shíyī yuè shíliù hào.
Wǒ shì yī jiǔ jiǔ bā nián shēng de.
Nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào?

ASGVH4Q5.explain: Days of the week are 星期 plus a number, Monday = 星期一. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日.

ASGCRH6P.explain: Numbers are built from 一 to 十: 11 is 十一, 20 is 二十, 21 is 二十一. A zero inside a number is said: 105 is 一百零五.

ASGN6BBU.explain: Clock times use 点 for the hour and 分 for minutes; 半 is half past.
examples: Wǒ bā diǎn shí fēn shàngkè.

ASGCI0KG.explain: With family members, close people and groups you belong to, 的 is usually dropped.

ASGUHQD2.explain: 的 marks possession, like 's or "of". The noun after 的 can be left out when it is clear.

ASGMJHZO.explain: 呢 after a noun asks "and what about …?", repeating the question just asked, or "where is …?".
examples: 你爸爸是老师，你妈妈呢？
Nǐ bàba shì lǎoshī, nǐ māma ne?
Your dad is a teacher; what about your mum?

ASGMPZ6D.explain: 吧 at the end softens a sentence into a suggestion: "let's …" or "why don't you …".

ASGLRWT8.explain: 在 as a verb says where someone or something is.
examples: Nǐ de shū zài zhuōzi shang.
Your book is on the table.

ASG04ZCI.explain: With a place first, 有 means "there is / there are".
examples: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì běn shū.
There is a book on the table.
Wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu hěn duō xuésheng.
There are many students in our school.

ASGUGWVZ.explain: 叫 gives someone's name: "to be called".

ASGFYNCL.explain: 去 means "to go (to)". The place comes straight after it, without "to".

ASGPS9NY.explain: 姓 gives the family name only. 您贵姓 is the polite question.

ASG9PQ40.explain: 能 is "can" in the sense of being able or free to do something now.

ASGRHM0E.explain: 会 is "can" for a learned skill: speaking a language, swimming, driving.

ASGVT2KN.explain: 要 before a verb can also mean "am going to", a plan or something about to happen.

ASG6SPYK.explain: 可以 is "may / can" for permission.
examples: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng wǒ de shǒujī.

ASGXVEAR.explain: 要 means "to want" (a thing, or to do something), more direct than 想.
examples: I want a glass of water.
I want to go to Beijing.

ASGH2MNO.explain: 怎么 asks "how" to do something. 你怎么了 means "what's wrong?".
examples: How do you write this character?
How do I get to the station?

ASGAUCXK.explain: Past actions that did not happen are negated with 没 (or 没有), not 不. No 了 is used after 没.
examples: I didn't go to school yesterday.

ASGIVZJU.explain: 不要 before a verb is "don't", a command.

ASGETNCO.explain: Time and place come before the verb, with time first.
examples: Wǒ míngtiān zài jiā kàn shū.
He ate at a restaurant yesterday.
我们晚上去电影院看电影。
Wǒmen wǎnshang qù diànyǐngyuàn kàn diànyǐng.
We're going to the cinema tonight.

ASGUN7RX.explain: 是 links two nouns: A is B. It is not used before adjectives (say 她很忙, not 她是忙).
examples: Zhè bú shì wǒ de shū.

ASG8HVFN.explain: 太…了 means "too …" or, with positive words, "so …!".

ASG17BLH.explain: Adjectives work as the predicate without 是. 很 is added as a neutral filler; without it the sentence sounds like a contrast ("she is tall, but …").

ASGZH7K3.explain: Repeating the verb or adjective with 不 in the middle makes a yes/no question. Don't add 吗 as well.

ASGJQPSC.pattern: question word in the answer's place
ASGJQPSC.explain: Question words (什么, 谁, 哪儿 …) sit exactly where the answer will go. The word order does not change.

ASG4D8XB.explain: 好不好 and 行不行 are tags meaning "OK?", a bit more insistent than 好吗.
examples: Wǒmen qù chīfàn, hǎo bu hǎo?
Nǐ bāng wǒ, xíng bu xíng?
Míngtiān zài shuō, hǎo bu hǎo?

ASGSJYZ2.explain: A short question tag at the end asks for agreement.
examples: Zhè shì nǐ de, shì ma?

ASGQ2AZA.explain: 吗 at the end turns a statement into a yes/no question. The word order does not change.

ASGJ46H1.explain: Before a measure word, "two" is 两, not 二. 二 is used when counting and inside numbers.

ASGLEVUV.explain: 死了 after an unpleasant adjective means "extremely", like "… to death".

ASG1NAXO.explain: 差不多 means "almost, about the same".
examples: These two are about the same.

ASGWNEYM.explain: 都 after a large or small amount stresses it: "as many as" or "even".
examples: Tā yí ge rén dōu bú rènshi.
He doesn't know a single person.
Wǒ sān tiān dōu méi shuìjiào.
I haven't slept for three whole days.
Even a hundred yuan isn't enough.

ASG846EA.explain: 在 or 正在 before a verb means the action is in progress right now.

ASGP000J.explain: 一直 means "all along, continuously", or "straight" for directions.
examples: I've been waiting for you the whole time.
Go straight on and you're there.

ASGNXI27.explain: 已经 means "already" and usually comes with 了.

ASGJBZKC.explain: 还 adds something more ("also, in addition") or says something is still going on.

ASGQJJYO.explain: 刚 before a verb means "just (a moment ago)".

ASGN8C8R.explain: 只 means "only" and goes before the verb.
examples: Wǒ zhǐ yǒu shí kuài qián.
Zhǐ yǒu yí ge rén lái le.

ASGEB54D.explain: 就 links two actions: "then / right after". It goes before the second verb.
examples: Xiàkè yǐhòu wǒ jiù huí jiā.
After class I'll go straight home.
We'll leave as soon as we've eaten.

ASG9W0UX.explain: 别 is the everyday "don't", like 不要.

ASG2ZC5S.explain: 一边…一边… means doing two things at the same time.
examples: 他一边吃饭一边看电视。
Tā yìbiān chīfàn yìbiān kàn diànshì.
Wǒ yìbiān zǒu yìbiān tīng yīnyuè.
I listen to music while walking.
别一边开车一边打电话。
Bié yìbiān kāichē yìbiān dǎ diànhuà.

ASG9LLJU.explain: 多 before an adjective asks "how …?": how big, how far, how long.
examples: How far is the station from here?
Nǐ xué le duō cháng shíjiān?

ASGC06N0.pattern: A + 和 / 跟 + B + 一样 (+ adjective)
ASGC06N0.explain: 一样 means "the same"; add an adjective for "as … as".
examples: These two books are the same.

ASGPM3MY.explain: 有点儿 before an adjective means "a bit", usually about something unwelcome. 一点儿 goes after an adjective and compares (贵一点儿).

ASGPFUM2.explain: 又…又… means "both … and …" for two qualities at once.
examples: Zhège cài yòu piányi yòu hǎochī.
This dish is both cheap and tasty.
The room is small and hot.

ASGI96BQ.pattern: A + 离 + B + 近 / 远
ASGI96BQ.explain: 离 gives the distance between two places.
examples: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
My home is close to school.
He is even taller than me.

ASGUNMHU.explain: 不太 means "not very", a soft negative.

ASGC885D.explain: 真 means "really" and shows feeling, often in exclamations.

ASGGH7RR.explain: 多 before an adjective in an exclamation means "how …!".

ASGAY164.explain: 还 before a positive adjective tones it down: "fairly, OK".

ASGVUFKX.explain: An adjective of two syllables, or one with 很, takes 的 before the noun. Short one-syllable adjectives usually don't: 好人, 新书.

ASGLQKD2.explain: A whole phrase can describe a noun; it goes before the noun with 的, where English uses "that/which …".

examples: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
This one is the most expensive.

ASG6HYOU.explain: 或者 is "or" in statements. In questions use 还是.
examples: We'll go tomorrow or the day after.
Nǐ kěyǐ hē chá huòzhě kāfēi.
You can have tea or coffee.
他或者在家，或者在公司。
Tā huòzhě zài jiā, huòzhě zài gōngsī.
He's either at home or at the office.

ASGSZ0HP.explain: 跟 means "with" (someone). The 跟 phrase goes before the verb.
examples: I'd like to have a chat with you.

ASG8VJM8.explain: 那个 (often nèige) is a filler while you think, like "um".
examples: Um… I'd like to ask something.
Tā shì nèige… wǒ de tóngshì.
Nèige, nǐ míngtiān yǒu kòng ma?

ASGUD81S.explain: 但是 and 可是 both mean "but"; 可是 is a little more spoken.
examples: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
I'd like to go, but I have no time.
Zhège hěn hǎo, kěshì tài guì le.
This is good, but too expensive.
Tā hěn cōngming, dànshì bù nǔlì.
He's clever but doesn't work hard.

ASGRLQGY.explain: 以后 comes after the time or event: "after …".
examples: After class we'll go and eat.
Sān diǎn yǐhòu wǒ yǒu shíjiān.
Huí jiā yǐhòu gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
Call me when you get home.

ASGJ2OJC.explain: 以前 comes after the time or event: "before …".
examples: 来中国以前我不会说中文。
Lái Zhōngguó yǐqián wǒ bú huì shuō Zhōngwén.
Before coming to China I couldn't speak Chinese.

ASGVCWLU.explain: 以前 at the start of a sentence means "in the past, before".
examples: I used to live in Shanghai.
There was no metro here before.
He used to be a teacher.

ASGQ1KOY.explain: 刚才 is a time word, "just now"; it can start the sentence. 刚 is an adverb and must go before the verb.
examples: I was in the shower just now.

ASGWN185.explain: 的时候 after a phrase means "when …".
examples: 我吃饭的时候不看手机。
Wǒ chīfàn de shíhou bú kàn shǒujī.
I don't look at my phone when eating.
Xià yǔ de shíhou wǒ zài jiā.
I was at home when it rained.
Xiǎo de shíhou wǒ zhù zài Běijīng.
When I was little I lived in Beijing.

ASGPVFU1.explain: 以后 at the start of a sentence means "in the future, from now on".
examples: In the future I want to be a doctor.
Don't be late from now on.

ASG5RWKO.explain: Time words go before the verb, either at the start of the sentence or right after the subject, never at the end.
examples: Tā měi tiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
He gets up at seven every morning.

ASGOUD8U.explain: Two neighbouring numbers together mean "about": 三四个 three or four.

ASGIM3AX.explain: Big numbers count in 万 (10,000) and 亿 (100 million): 100,000 is 十万, one million is 一百万.

ASGDTO07.explain: 一刻 is a quarter hour, 三刻 three quarters; 差 gives minutes to the hour.

ASGHC9CA.explain: 几 in a statement means "several, a few".

ASGT185D.explain: 了 at the end of a sentence marks a change: a new situation that is true now.

ASGJIP2E.explain: 吧 can show reluctant agreement: "fine, OK then".
examples: Let's leave it at that, then.

ASGM055L.explain: A sentence-final 了 after a plain verb says the action has happened: "already".

ASGAGDCQ.explain: 了 right after the verb marks the action as completed. The object usually carries a number or a modifier; with a bare object, people add a second 了 at the end (我吃饭了).
examples: Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.
Tā hē le sān bēi kāfēi.
He drank three cups of coffee.
Zuótiān wǒ kàn le yí ge diànyǐng.

ASGQGV3P.explain: 过 after a verb says you have had the experience at some point ("have ever …"). Negate with 没 and keep 过. Compare 了, which marks one completed event.
examples: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?
ASGQGV3P.note: 过 is read in the neutral tone here (guo).

ASGFR96B.explain: 不…了 means "not … anymore": something that was planned or usual stops.

ASGE5Q4J.explain: 了 at the end can mean a situation is true now, often with 现在 or 已经.

ASGC8CB8.explain: 呢 at the end of a statement adds a lively tone, often with 在 or 还 for something going on.

ASGW66JM.explain: 啊 at the end adds emotion: surprise, warmth or emphasis.

ASGDHC1H.explain: 吧 after a statement makes it a soft guess: "…, right?".

ASG5MOMM.pattern: 的 · 得 · 地 (the three de)
ASG5MOMM.explain: Three particles are all read de. 的 links a modifier to a noun (红色的车). 得 goes after a verb and links it to a comment on how it was done (跑得很快). 地 turns an adjective into an adverb before a verb (慢慢地走).

ASGP69JD.explain: 过 with 了 means something has already been done, so it doesn't need doing again.
examples: 这个问题我们讨论过了。
Wǒ qùguo le, bù xiǎng zài qù.
I've already been; I don't want to go again.

ASG8SI2K.explain: 比 compares: A is more … than B. Don't put 很 before the adjective; use 一点儿 or 得多 after it for "a bit" or "much".
examples: This one is a bit more expensive than that one.

ASGGGIW8.explain: 从…到… means "from … to …", for places and times.
examples: 我从八点到十二点上课。
Wǒ cóng bā diǎn dào shí'èr diǎn shàngkè.
I have class from eight to twelve.
从早上到晚上他都在工作。
Cóng zǎoshang dào wǎnshang tā dōu zài gōngzuò.
He works from morning till night.

ASGEAH5M.explain: 没有 compares the other way: A is not as … as B.
examples: I'm not as tall as him.
This isn't as tasty as that.
Beijing isn't as hot as Shanghai.

ASGRBKSL.explain: 来 is movement towards the speaker, 去 away from the speaker.

ASG25C48.explain: 请 before a verb makes a polite request: "please …".
examples: Excuse me, where is the toilet?
Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi shuǐ.
Please give me a glass of water.

ASG95AL1.explain: 要 has several meanings: to want, to be going to, and "must" (要小心). Context decides.

examples: We should leave a bit earlier.

ASGW9737.explain: 会 can also mean "will", a prediction. A final 的 adds certainty.
examples: Nǐ huì xǐhuan zhège diànyǐng de.

ASGT97VF.explain: 想 before a verb is "would like to", softer than 要.
examples: I'd like to go to China.
What would you like to eat?

ASGPRGAX.explain: Two actions in a row just follow each other; the second gives the purpose: go somewhere to do something.
examples: I'm going to the shop to buy things.
He came to Beijing to study Chinese.
We're going to a restaurant to eat.

ASG35T4H.explain: 难 before a verb means "hard to": 难懂 hard to understand, 难看 ugly, 难吃 bad-tasting.
examples: This character is hard to write.
Tā de huà hěn nán dǒng.
What he says is hard to understand.

ASGJ36VN.explain: The length of time goes after the verb; 了 marks that the period is over.
examples: Wǒ xué le liǎng nián Zhōngwén.
I studied Chinese for two years.
Tā shuì le shí ge xiǎoshí.
Wǒmen děng le bàn ge xiǎoshí.

ASG8NM5E.pattern: 从来 + 不 / 没 + verb
ASG8NM5E.explain: 从来不 means "never" (habit); 从来没…过 means "have never".

ASG69RR8.explain: A second 了 at the end means the action is still going on: "have been … for".
examples: Wǒ xué le liǎng nián Zhōngwén le.
I've been studying Chinese for two years.
Tā zài Běijīng zhù le wǔ nián le.
He's been living in Beijing for five years.
Wǒmen děng le yí ge xiǎoshí le.
We've been waiting for an hour.

ASGNVE15.pattern: A + 和 / 跟 + B + 一起 + verb
ASGNVE15.explain: 一起 means "together" and goes before the verb.
examples: 你想跟我们一起吃饭吗？
Nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chīfàn ma?
Would you like to eat with us?

ASGI2KHC.explain: 没办法 means "there's no way, can't help it".
examples: There's no way I can help you.
Can't be helped; it's too expensive.
He has no way of coming.

ASGX0Z0N.explain: Where an action happens is given with 在 before the verb, not after it.

ASGYC77J.explain: Repeating a verb makes it light and casual: "have a look", "take a little rest".
examples: Let me think for a moment.

ASG90DXK.explain: With verbs of placing or staying (放, 住, 坐, 站), 在 + place comes after the verb.
examples: Put the book on the table.

ASGID0E8.pattern: 很 + 喜欢 / 想 / 怕 …
ASGID0E8.explain: A few feeling verbs (喜欢, 想, 怕, 希望, 了解) take 很 like adjectives.

ASGLFX54.explain: 到 as a verb means "to arrive (at)".
examples: When do you get to Beijing?

ASGJQU93.explain: 好 before a verb means "easy to" or "good to": 好吃 tasty, 好看 nice-looking, 好找 easy to find.
examples: This place is easy to find.
This book is a good read.

ASGWCESP.explain: 一下 after a verb means "briefly, a little", and softens requests.

ASGI2OAG.explain: A few verbs (给, 教, 问, 告诉, 送) take two objects: the person first, then the thing.
examples: Tā gěi wǒ yì běn shū.
Wǒ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí.
Let me ask you a question.

ASG8R2V8.explain: 听不懂 / 看不懂 mean you can't understand what you hear or read; 听得懂 is the positive.
examples: Zhège zì wǒ kàn bu dǒng.

ASGWNGEP.explain: 到 and 见 after a verb say the action reached its goal: 看见 saw, 听到 heard, 找到 found.
examples: Wǒ zhǎodào wǒ de yàoshi le.

ASGNQUC1.explain: 完 after a verb means the action is finished.
examples: Kànwán zhè běn shū zài shuō.
Let's talk after you finish this book.
Zhèxiē shū li yǒu yìxiē hěn jiù.
Some of these books are very old.

ASG4NDHB.explain: 有的 means "some (of them)", often repeated: some …, others ….
examples: 有的人喜欢茶，有的人喜欢咖啡。
Yǒude rén xǐhuan chá, yǒude rén xǐhuan kāfēi.
Some people like tea, others coffee.

ASGL6JOE.explain: Money is counted in 块 (yuan) and 毛 (tenths) in speech; 元 and 角 in writing.

ASGB6L4M.pattern: 每 + measure word + noun + 都
ASGB6L4M.explain: 每 means "every" and is usually paired with 都 before the verb.
examples: Měi nián xiàtiān wǒ dōu huí jiā.

ASGAC1P9.pattern: number + measure word + 半 / 半 + measure word
ASGAC1P9.explain: 半 means half: 半个 half a, 一个半 one and a half.

ASG64BTE.explain: Many nouns have their own measure word: 本 for books, 杯 for cups, 件 for clothes, 只 for animals, 张 for flat things.

ASGL9KQM.pattern: 几 / 多少 + measure word + noun？
ASGL9KQM.explain: 几 asks about small numbers and needs a measure word; 多少 asks about any number and the measure word is optional.
examples: How many children do you have?
How many people are in your class?

ASGZC42B.pattern: 这 / 那 + measure word + noun
ASGZC42B.explain: 这 and 那 take a measure word before the noun: 这本书, 那个人.
examples: I'll take this one (piece of clothing).

ASGK904U.explain: 第 before a number makes it ordinal: first, second, third.
examples: Zhè shì wǒ dì-èr cì lái Běijīng.
This is my second time in Beijing.

ASGC701A.explain: 怎么样 asks "how is it?" or "how about …?".
examples: How about we go and eat?

ASGD7NS3.explain: 怎么 can also ask "how come?", with surprise.

ASGYKDNF.explain: 了吗 asks whether something has happened yet. Answer with 了 or 没有.

ASGTDUJO.explain: 因为 gives the reason, 所以 the result. Unlike English, both are usually used together.
examples: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù.
Because it rained, I didn't go.
因为他病了，所以没来上课。
Yīnwèi tā bìng le, suǒyǐ méi lái shàngkè.
He didn't come to class because he was ill.
Wǒ hěn lèi, suǒyǐ zǎo diǎn shuì.
I'm tired, so I'll go to bed early.

ASGNGEU8.explain: 要…了 and 快…了 say something is about to happen.
examples: The train is about to leave.

ASGAQV6C.pattern: 什么 + 都 / 也 + verb
ASGAQV6C.explain: 什么都 means "everything"; 什么都不 / 没 means "nothing".

ASGFBWZL.pattern: 在 + place + 上 / 下 / 里
ASGFBWZL.explain: 上, 下 and 里 after a place word mean on, under and in.
examples: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the chair.

ASGZ8OIF.explain: 别…了 tells someone to stop doing what they are doing.

ASGRJ1BI.explain: 不 is for the present, the future, habits and wishes; 没 is for what did not happen or has not happened yet.
examples: Tā bù xǐhuan, yě méi mǎi.
He didn't like it and didn't buy it.

ASGD88UO.explain: 想 is "would like to", a wish; 要 is "want / am going to", firmer.
examples: I'd like to go to China.
I'm going to China. / I want to go to China.
What would you like to drink?

ASGVME5V.explain: 极了 after an adjective means "extremely".

ASGVYIZT.explain: 不怎么 means "not very, not really".

ASGCPDSR.explain: 全 means "whole, all", often with 都.

ASGDHE8S.explain: Repeating an adjective (高高, 干干净净) makes it vivid; such forms take 的 before a noun and 地 before a verb.

ASGMAFSX.explain: Adjectives become adverbs before a verb, usually with 地 for two-syllable ones.

ASGUD25J.explain: 正好 means "just right, by coincidence".
examples: He happened to be there too.
Nǐ hái zhù zài nàr ma?

ASGY21RK.explain: 就是 stresses "exactly, precisely", or insists.
examples: I just don't want to go.

ASGD3C4S.explain: 又 before a negation stresses it: "it's not as if …".
examples: I'm not a child, you know.
It's not as if he said anything wrong.

ASG9B210.explain: 就要…了 means "about to", a bit sooner than 要…了.
examples: The train is about to leave.

ASGIZQJ2.explain: 再 means "again" for something not yet done. For something that already happened again, use 又.

ASGN1JR5.explain: 又 means "again" for something that has already happened again.

ASGTKXFR.explain: 原来 means "originally" or, discovering something, "so it turns out that".
examples: It turns out he's a teacher.

ASG06EA8.explain: 一下子 means "all at once, in an instant".
examples: The money was gone in a flash.

ASG6ESWW.explain: 差点儿 means "almost" (but it didn't happen).

ASGT1CIR.explain: 都 before a time or amount means "already", with a note of surprise.
examples: Dōu zhème wǎn le, kuài shuì ba.
It's so late already; go to sleep.

ASG8KUHG.explain: 从来 with a positive verb means "always have".

ASG6B21A.explain: 结果 introduces the outcome: "as a result, in the end".
examples: Tā méi fùxí, jiéguǒ méi kǎohǎo.
He didn't revise; as a result he did badly.
我们等了很久，结果他没来。
Wǒmen děng le hěn jiǔ, jiéguǒ tā méi lái.
We waited a long time, and in the end he didn't come.

ASGSVF28.explain: A time span before 没 says how long something has not happened.
examples: Wǒ sān tiān méi shuìjiào le.
I haven't slept for three days.
Tā hěn jiǔ méi lái le.
He hasn't been here for ages.
Wǒmen yì nián méi jiàn le.
We haven't seen each other for a year.

ASGKITRZ.explain: 就 says something happened earlier or sooner than expected.
examples: Tā liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
He was up as early as six.
Tā èrshí suì jiù jiéhūn le.

ASGWAR65.explain: 还是 can suggest the better choice: "had better".

ASG35CD7.explain: 最好 means "had better, it would be best to".
examples: You'd better go to bed early.

ASG1F4D1.explain: 这样 means "like this, in this way"; 这样 at the start of a clause means "that way, then".
examples: You should do it like this.
早点出发，这样不会迟到。
Zǎo diǎn chūfā, zhèyàng bú huì chídào.
Leave early; that way you won't be late.

ASG3WTCJ.explain: 才 says something happened later than expected, or only then. Compare 就 for earlier than expected.
examples: He didn't get up until ten.

ASGBC7A0.pattern: 一 + measure word + 一 + measure word
ASGBC7A0.explain: 一…一… with a measure word means "one by one".
examples: Tā yí bù yí bù de zǒu.
Wǒ yí yè yí yè de kàn.
I read it page by page.

ASGPW8PP.explain: 就 before a quantity stresses that it is small: "only".
examples: Tā jiù lái le yí cì.

ASGLJM55.explain: 先…再… puts actions in order: first …, then ….
examples: Eat first, then do your homework.
Nǐ xiān zǒu, wǒ zài lái.
You go first; I'll come later.
我们先去商店，然后回家。
Wǒmen xiān qù shāngdiàn, ránhòu huí jiā.
We'll go to the shop first, then home.

ASGII66E.explain: 老是 means "always" as a complaint.

ASGYW5RS.explain: 才 before a number stresses that it is small: "only".
examples: Lái le cái sān ge rén.

ASG8GSXY.explain: 也 and 都 can be used together, in that order: "also all".
examples: Zhèxiē yě dōu shì nǐ de.

ASGNKKP6.explain: 这么 and 那么 mean "so, this/that …".

ASGDIDAC.explain: 什么的 after a list means "and so on, and the like".
examples: 我买了水果、面包什么的。
Wǒ mǎi le shuǐguǒ, miànbāo shénme de.
I bought fruit, bread and so on.
他喜欢打球、游泳什么的。
Tā xǐhuan dǎqiú, yóuyǒng shénme de.
He likes ball games, swimming and that sort of thing.
他喜欢历史、文学之类的书。
Tā xǐhuan lìshǐ, wénxué zhīlèi de shū.
He likes books on history, literature and the like.
Kāfēi zhīlèi de wǒ bù hē.
I don't drink coffee and things like that.

ASGF763H.explain: 等 or 等等 ends a list: "etc.".
examples: big cities such as Beijing and Shanghai
我们学了听、说、读、写等等。
Wǒmen xué le tīng, shuō, dú, xiě děngděng.
We studied listening, speaking, reading, writing and so on.

ASGA0S4T.explain: 不过 is a softer "but, however".
examples: Wǒ xiǎng qù, búguò tài yuǎn le.
I'd like to go; it's too far, though.
菜很好吃，不过有点儿贵。
Cài hěn hǎochī, búguò yǒudiǎnr guì.
The food is good, though a bit pricey.
Kuài zǒu, yàobù jiù wǎn le.

ASGHQRI1.explain: 还有 adds one more thing: "and also".
examples: I'd like coffee, and cake too.
Háiyǒu, bié wàng le dài qián.
Also, don't forget to bring money.

ASG2KQZI.explain: 另外 at the start of a sentence means "in addition, besides".
examples: Lìngwài, wǒ hái yǒu yí ge wèntí.
We also need to buy water.

ASGATDLX.explain: 再说 adds another reason: "besides, what's more".
examples: 太贵了，再说我也不需要。
Tài guì le, zàishuō wǒ yě bù xūyào.
It's too expensive; besides, I don't need it.
Bié qù le, zàishuō tiān yě wǎn le.
Don't go; what's more, it's late.
Wǒ méi shíjiān, zàishuō yě méi qián.
I have no time, and no money either.

ASGX298Z.explain: 那么 at the start of a sentence means "then, in that case".
examples: Nǐ bú qù, nàme wǒ yě bú qù.
If you're not going, then I'm not either.

ASGBZ578.explain: 来 can link a means and a purpose: do A to do B.
examples: Wǒ yòng shǒujī lái xué Zhōngwén.
I use my phone to learn Chinese.
Wǒmen zuò chē lái shěng shíjiān.
We take the bus to save time.

ASG6120A.explain: A doubled measure word means "every": 个个 everyone, 天天 every day.
examples: Every one of them is clever.

ASGTD3L3.explain: 之前 and 之后 are like 以前 and 以后, a little more formal.
examples: After class I go to the library.

ASGNEMXP.explain: 以来 means "since (a time) until now".
examples: Qùnián yǐlái tā yìzhí hěn máng.
He's been busy ever since last year.
三个月以来我每天学中文。
Sān ge yuè yǐlái wǒ měi tiān xué Zhōngwén.
For the past three months I've studied Chinese daily.

ASGGL59D.explain: 时 after a phrase means "when", a written form of 的时候.
examples: Xià yǔ shí lù hěn huá.
When it rains the road is slippery.
Turn off the light when you leave.

ASGY0UDC.explain: 后来 means "later, afterwards" for past events.
examples: 他先在北京，后来去了上海。
Tā xiān zài Běijīng, hòulái qù le Shànghǎi.
He was in Beijing first, then later went to Shanghai.

ASG84RE9.explain: Fractions say the denominator first: 三分之一 one third, 百分之十 ten per cent.
examples: sì fēn zhī yī de xuésheng

ASG004ZK.explain: 多 or 几 after a round number means "more than": 十多个 over ten, 二十几 twenty-odd.

ASGI9WXT.explain: Other tags like 不是吗, 行吗, 可以吗 check or ask for agreement.
examples: Nǐ zǎo jiù zhīdào le, bú shì ma?
You knew long ago, didn't you?
我用一下你的电脑，行吗？
Wǒ yòng yíxià nǐ de diànnǎo, xíng ma?
Can I use your computer for a moment?

ASGOIDEO.explain: 着 after a verb marks a continuing state: the door is open, he is wearing a coat. With two verbs, V1着 V2 means doing V2 while in state V1 (笑着说). Negate with 没.
examples: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn hóng yīfu.
ASGOIDEO.note: 着 is read in the neutral tone here (zhe). Compare 在 + verb for an action in progress: 他在穿衣服 (he's putting clothes on) vs 他穿着红衣服 (he has a red top on).

ASGVMC4B.explain: 嘛 at the end says something is obvious: "of course, you know".

ASGELOTT.explain: 吧 after each option weighs them up: "if A, …; if B, …".
examples: 去吧，太远；不去吧，又想见他。
Qù ba, tài yuǎn; bú qù ba, yòu xiǎng jiàn tā.
Go, and it's too far; don't go, and I still want to see him.
买吧，太贵；不买吧，很喜欢。
Mǎi ba, tài guì; bù mǎi ba, hěn xǐhuan.
Buying it is too expensive; not buying it, I really like it.
Say it, and I'm afraid he'll get angry.

ASG19S1M.explain: 的 at the end of a statement adds certainty: "for sure". Often with 会.

examples: 关于这个问题，我们明天谈。
Guānyú zhège wèntí, wǒmen míngtiān tán.
We'll talk about this question tomorrow.
一本关于中国历史的书
yì běn guānyú Zhōngguó lìshǐ de shū
Guānyú tā, wǒ bú tài liǎojiě.
I don't know much about him.

ASGC6E1C.explain: 直到 means "until, all the way until".
examples: Wǒ zhídào shí'èr diǎn cái shuì.
Tā zhídào xiànzài hái méi lái.

ASGLHAV3.explain: 给 before the verb means "for" someone: doing something on their behalf or for their benefit.
examples: Tā gěi wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.

ASG68RBX.explain: 为 means "for (the sake of)", a bit more formal than 给.
examples: Tā wèi zhè jiàn shì hěn dānxīn.

ASG10CAE.explain: 不到 before a number means "less than".
examples: Bú dào shí ge rén lái le.
Bú dào wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
We got there in under five minutes.

ASGQXARS.explain: 向 means "towards", for directions and for actions aimed at someone.

examples: Zhè tàng chē kāi wǎng Shànghǎi.

ASGH13JY.explain: 在 also works with abstract places: 在…方面 in terms of, 在…上 in, 在…下 under.
examples: Zài gōngzuò shang tā hěn rènzhēn.
Zài zhè fāngmiàn wǒ méiyǒu jīngyàn.
In this area I have no experience.

ASG8ICO9.explain: 对 means "to, towards" with verbs like 说, 笑, 好, and "about" with 感兴趣.
examples: Wǒ duì yīnyuè hěn gǎn xìngqù.
Zhège cài kàn qǐlái hěn hǎochī.
Tā kàn qǐlái sānshí duō suì.

ASG5T7XC.pattern: 让 / 叫 / 请 + person + verb
ASG5T7XC.explain: 让, 叫 and 请 make someone do something: let, tell, ask.
examples: Mum told me to come home.
The teacher told us to be quiet.
Whether we go depends on the weather.
She doesn't seem to know me.

ASGRBC43.explain: 以为 means "thought (mistakenly)". For a correct opinion use 觉得 or 认为.
examples: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù lái le.
Wǒ yǐwéi zhè shì nǐ de.

ASG11DA8.explain: 经过 means "to pass by" or "through (a process)".
examples: Wǒ měi tiān jīngguò nà jiā diàn.
I pass that shop every day.

ASG9B1E3.explain: 通过 means "by means of, through" (also "to pass" an exam).
examples: Wǒ tōngguò péngyou rènshi le tā.
I met her through a friend.
Tōngguò xuéxí, wǒ dǒng le hěn duō.
Through studying I learned a lot.

ASG1CEA8.explain: 来自 means "to come from", slightly formal.
examples: 这些学生来自不同的国家。
Zhèxiē xuésheng láizì bùtóng de guójiā.
These students come from different countries.
Where does the problem come from?

ASGWDWFN.explain: 算 means "counts as, can be considered".
examples: He counts as a friend of mine.

ASG98FZK.explain: 来 can stand in for a verb that is clear from context: "let me (do it)".

ASGPXLP9.explain: 得, read děi, means "must, have to" in speech. Its negative is 不用, not 不得.

ASG9B0M8.explain: 少 before a verb means "do less".

ASGLKGZP.explain: 多 before a verb means "do more".

ASGEYQ9O.explain: The full progressive is 正在 + verb + 呢; 正, 在 and 呢 can each be dropped.

ASG5BOGP.explain: 不怎么 before a verb means "not often, not much".

ASG1CCAP.explain: 到 after a verb means "until" a time or "to" a place.

ASG5AODR.pattern: verb + number + 次 / 遍 / 下
ASG5AODR.explain: How many times an action is done goes after the verb: 次 times, 遍 times through from start to end, 下 brief actions.
examples: Please read it through once more.
Tā qiāo le sān xià mén.
He knocked on the door three times.

ASG4GVRX.explain: Separable verbs like 睡觉, 见面, 帮忙 are verb + object; 了, 过, a duration or a measure go between the two parts.
examples: Wǒ shuì le bā ge xiǎoshí jiào.
Tā bāng le wǒ hěn duō máng.

ASGMMHTQ.explain: 给 after verbs like 送, 卖, 借, 寄 says who receives.
examples: Wǒ sòng gěi tā yì běn shū.
I gave him a book as a present.
Tā mài gěi wǒ yí liàng chē.

ASG3ORNN.explain: 给 before verbs like 打电话, 写信, 发 says who receives.
examples: Tā gěi wǒ fā le duǎnxìn.

ASG79STE.explain: 得 after a verb introduces a comment on how the action is done. If there is an object, say the verb twice: 她唱歌唱得很好. Negate after 得 (得不好), ask with 得怎么样.
ASG79STE.note: 得 is read in the neutral tone here (de); as a verb it is dé (get) or děi (must).

ASG8LWBJ.pattern: verb + 进来 / 出去 / 上 / 下 …
ASG8LWBJ.explain: Direction words after a verb say which way the movement goes; 来 and 去 add towards or away from the speaker.

ASGBPXOB.explain: 起来 means upward movement, the start of something, or "seems" with 看/听/闻.

ASGCPJPQ.explain: 得 or 不 between a verb and its complement says whether the result is possible: 吃得完 can finish eating, 吃不完 can't finish.

ASGNNMST.pattern: verb + result (好, 错, 清楚, 住 …)
ASGNNMST.explain: A second word after the verb gives the result of the action: 做错 do wrongly, 写好 finish writing properly, 听清楚 hear clearly, 记住 remember firmly.

ASG1PTJX.explain: 下去 after a verb means "to go on, continue".

ASGOWBSL.explain: 所有 means "all", usually with 的 and 都.
examples: Suǒyǒu de rén dōu lái le.
Wǒ kàn le suǒyǒu de shū.
Suǒyǒu de wèntí dōu jiějué le.
他是我最好的朋友之一。
Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou zhī yī.
He's one of my best friends.
北京是中国最大的城市之一。
Běijīng shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de chéngshì zhī yī.
Beijing is one of China's biggest cities.
This is one of the reasons.

ASGD3FE5.explain: 另外 before a measure word means "the other, another".
examples: Lìngwài yí ge rén shì shéi?
Lìngwài liǎng běn shū zài zhèr.
The other two books are here.

ASGD4EC8.explain: 不是…吗 is a rhetorical question: "isn't it the case that …?".
examples: Nǐ bú shì shuō nǐ bù lái ma?
Didn't you say you weren't coming?
Zhè bú shì hěn jiǎndān ma?
Tā bú shì nǐ péngyou ma?

ASGE662E.pattern: subject + 是 + detail + verb + 的
ASGE662E.explain: 是…的 stresses one detail (when, where, how, who) of something that already happened. 是 goes before the detail, 的 after the verb.
examples: It was yesterday that I came.
Tā shì zài Běijīng chūshēng de.
It wasn't me who said it.

ASG0UFR4.pattern: 是 + 来 / 为了 … 的
ASG0UFR4.explain: 是…的 can state the purpose or reason of a situation.
examples: 他是为了工作来北京的。
Tā shì wèile gōngzuò lái Běijīng de.
He came to Beijing for work.

ASG8YTSF.explain: 是…的 has several uses: stressing a detail of a past event (我是坐飞机来的), stating purpose or reason (我是来学习的), and adding certainty (他会来的).
examples: Wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de.
Zhè shì wǒ zìjǐ zuò de.

ASG5KNWW.explain: Chinese often puts the topic first, then comments on it, even if the topic is the object.

ASG2UB2B.explain: 把 moves the object before the verb to say what was done to it. The verb must have something after it (了, a result, a direction, a place). Not used with 是, 有, 喜欢 or 知道. 没 and 别 go before 把.
examples: Tā bǎ wǒ de shū názǒu le.
Bié bǎ shǒujī wàng zài jiā li.
Don't leave your phone at home.

ASGHF9F1.explain: 被 makes a passive: the subject has something done to it. The doer after 被 can be left out. Often used for unpleasant events. Negate with 没 before 被.
examples: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
He was told off by the teacher.
The cake was eaten up by my little brother.

ASGAC619.explain: A place can come first with 着 to describe what is there: on the wall hangs a picture.
examples: Qiáng shang guàzhe yì zhāng huà.
A picture hangs on the wall.
Zhuōzi shang fàngzhe yì běn shū.
A book is lying on the table.
Someone is standing at the door.

ASGDUZ55.explain: Repeating a question word with 就 means "whatever / whenever you like".
examples: Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme jiù chī shénme.
Xiǎng qù nǎr jiù qù nǎr.
Whoever wants to speak may speak.

ASGEEA2D.explain: Two negatives make a strong positive: 不得不 have to, 没有不 all.
examples: I have no choice but to go.

ASGNP0WV.pattern: 连 + noun + 都 / 也 + verb
ASGNP0WV.explain: 连…都… means "even …", stressing an extreme case.
examples: Tā lián yí ge zì dōu bú rènshi.
He doesn't know even one character.
Wǒ lián fàn dōu méi chī.
Tā měi cì lái dōu dài lǐwù.
Every time he comes he brings a gift.
Wǒ měi cì kǎoshì dōu jǐnzhāng.
Měi cì xià yǔ dōu dǔchē.
Every time it rains there's a traffic jam.

ASG13ALM.explain: A question word with 都 means "every / any": 谁都 everyone, 哪儿都 everywhere.

ASGCED31.explain: Frequency: the time span first, then how many times.
examples: Wǒ yí ge xīngqī qù liǎng cì.
Tā měi tiān chī sān cì yào.
He takes medicine three times a day.
Nǐ duō jiǔ huí yí cì jiā?
How often do you go home?
The weather is getting colder and colder.
His Chinese is getting better and better.
I like it here more and more.

ASG7D4EC.pattern: A + 比 + B + adjective + number + 倍
ASG7D4EC.explain: 倍 expresses multiples: 两倍 twice as much.
examples: Zhège bǐ nàge guì liǎng bèi.
This is twice as expensive as that.
Tā de gōngzī shì wǒ de sān bèi.
His salary is three times mine.

ASGRURCZ.pattern: 一点儿 + 也 / 都 + 不 / 没
ASGRURCZ.explain: 一点儿也不 means "not at all".

ASG0EQQJ.pattern: 不知道 + 怎么 + verb + 好
ASG0EQQJ.explain: 不知道怎么…好 means "don't know what to do / how best to".
examples: Wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme bàn hǎo.
I don't know what to do.
Wǒ bù zhīdào shuō shénme hǎo.
I don't know what to say.
I don't know where would be best to go.

ASGQGJXT.explain: 为了 gives the purpose: "in order to, for the sake of".
examples: 为了学中文，他去了中国。
Wèile xué Zhōngwén, tā qù le Zhōngguó.
He went to China to learn Chinese.
Wèile jiànkāng, wǒ měi tiān pǎobù.
For my health I run every day.
This is for your own good.

ASG7ED89.explain: In statements, question words can mean "some/any": 什么 something, 谁 someone.
examples: Nǐ xiǎng chī diǎnr shénme ma?
Do you want something to eat?
Hǎoxiàng yǒu shéi zài qiāo mén.

ASGD60A6.explain: 对…来说 means "for …, as far as … is concerned".
examples: Duì wǒ láishuō, Hànzì zuì nán.
For me, characters are the hardest.
Duì xuésheng láishuō zhè tài guì le.
For students this is too expensive.

ASG5DG95.pattern: A + 有 + B + (这么 / 那么) + adjective
ASG5DG95.explain: 有 compares as "as … as", often in questions or with 这么 / 那么.
examples: Is he as tall as you?
I'm not as busy as him.
Zhèr yǒu Běijīng nàme lěng ma?
Is it as cold here as in Beijing?
Gēn tā bǐ, wǒ chà yuǎn le.
Compared with him, I'm way behind.
Gēn qùnián bǐ, jīnnián rè duō le.
Compared with last year, this year is much hotter.
Gēn Běijīng bǐ, zhèr hěn ānjìng.
Compared with Beijing, it's quiet here.

ASG64E96.pattern: A + 比 + B + 更 / 还 + adjective
ASG64E96.explain: 更 or 还 before the adjective in a 比 sentence means "even more".
examples: He is even taller than me.
Today is even hotter than yesterday.
This is even better than that.

ASG6KUS5.pattern: A + 比 + B + adjective + 多了 / 得多
ASG6KUS5.explain: 多了 or 得多 after the adjective means "much more".
examples: Tā bǐ wǒ gāo duō le.
Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng de duō.
Today is much colder than yesterday.
Zhège bǐ nàge piányi duō le.
This is much cheaper than that.

ASGT9Y8P.explain: Repeating with 是 concedes a point: "it is …, but".
examples: Hǎo shì hǎo, dànshì tài guì le.
It's good, all right, but too expensive.
Xiǎng shì xiǎng qù, kěshì méi shíjiān.
I do want to go, but I have no time.
他聪明是聪明，就是不努力。
Tā cōngming shì cōngming, jiùshì bù nǔlì.
Clever he is, but he doesn't work hard.

ASGTFUD0.explain: 一…就… means "as soon as A, B".
examples: Wǒ yí dào jiā jiù shuìjiào.
I go to sleep as soon as I get home.
He understands as soon as he looks.
一下课我就给你打电话。
Yí xiàkè wǒ jiù gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
I'll call you as soon as class ends.

ASGXI560.explain: 虽然…但是… is "although …, (but) …". Both words are used together.
examples: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì hěn gāoxìng.
虽然他是中国人，但是不会写汉字。
Suīrán tā shì Zhōngguórén, dànshì bú huì xiě Hànzì.
Although he's Chinese, he can't write characters.
虽然下雨，我们还是去了。
Suīrán xià yǔ, wǒmen háishi qù le.
Although it rained, we still went.
Yàome nǐ lái, yàome wǒ qù.
Either you come, or I go.
要么现在走，要么别走了。
Yàome xiànzài zǒu, yàome bié zǒu le.
Either leave now or don't leave at all.
Either take the bus or walk.

ASGHFPGG.explain: 除了…以外 means "except" with 都, or "besides, in addition to" with 还 / 也.
examples: 除了小王以外，大家都来了。
Chúle Xiǎo Wáng yǐwài, dàjiā dōu lái le.
Chúle Zhōngwén, tā hái huì Rìyǔ.
Besides Chinese, he also knows Japanese.
除了周末，我每天都工作。
Chúle zhōumò, wǒ měi tiān dōu gōngzuò.
I work every day except weekends.

ASGOB1BF.explain: 还好 means "luckily, fortunately" (or "not bad" as an answer).
examples: Good thing I brought an umbrella.

ASGGIVT0.explain: 如果 means "if"; 就 introduces the result.
examples: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去。
Rúguǒ míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù.
If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
如果你有时间，就来找我。
Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu shíjiān, jiù lái zhǎo wǒ.
If you have time, come and find me.
Rúguǒ tài guì, wǒ jiù bù mǎi.
If it's too expensive, I won't buy it.

ASGN4VUU.explain: 的话 closes an "if" clause; 如果 can then be dropped.
examples: 如果你有时间的话，来找我。
Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu shíjiān dehuà, lái zhǎo wǒ.
If you have time, come and find me.
Tài guì dehuà, wǒ jiù bù mǎi.
If it's too expensive, I won't buy it.

ASGTYJ3E.explain: 不但…而且… means "not only …, but also …".
examples: 他不但会说中文，而且说得很好。
Tā búdàn huì shuō Zhōngwén, érqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
He not only speaks Chinese, but speaks it well.
这个菜不但好吃，而且便宜。
Zhège cài búdàn hǎochī, érqiě piányi.
This dish is not only tasty but cheap.
她不但聪明，而且很努力。
Tā búdàn cōngming, érqiě hěn nǔlì.
She's not only clever but hard-working.
Nánguài tā méi lái, tā bìng le.
No wonder he didn't come; he's ill.

ASGCWHNF.explain: 一方面…另一方面… means "on the one hand …, on the other …".
examples: 一方面想去，另一方面又怕累。
Yì fāngmiàn xiǎng qù, lìng yì fāngmiàn yòu pà lèi.
On the one hand I want to go; on the other I'm afraid it'll be tiring.
一方面要工作，另一方面要学习。
Yì fāngmiàn yào gōngzuò, lìng yì fāngmiàn yào xuéxí.
On the one hand I have to work, on the other I have to study.
这一方面省钱，另一方面省时间。
Zhè yì fāngmiàn shěng qián, lìng yì fāngmiàn shěng shíjiān.
This saves money on the one hand and time on the other.

ASG68F61.explain: 等到 (or 等) means "when, by the time".
examples: Děngdào nǐ huílái, wǒ zài shuō.
I'll tell you when you're back.
Děngdào míngnián wǒ jiù bìyè le.
By next year I'll have graduated.
Děng wǒ yǒu qián le, jiù mǎi chē.
When I have money I'll buy a car.

ASGE8FLP.explain: Both mean "often"; 经常 is a bit more formal and can be negated (不经常), 常常 is negated as 不常.

ASGJFFWG.explain: 刚 is an adverb ("just") before the verb; 刚才 is a time noun ("a moment ago") and can start the sentence or take 的.
examples: He was here a moment ago.
Gāngcái de shì bié gàosu tā.
Don't tell him what just happened.

ASGV55Y4.pattern: 有点儿 + adj · adj + 一点儿
ASGV55Y4.explain: 有点儿 goes before an adjective ("a bit", negative feel); 一点儿 goes after it to compare ("a bit more").
examples: Is there a slightly smaller one?
Today is a bit colder than yesterday.

ASGZL717.explain: 会: a learned skill (会游泳). 能: being able or free to, given the circumstances (今天不能来). 可以: permission (可以进来吗).
examples: 我会游泳，但是今天不能游。
Wǒ huì yóuyǒng, dànshì jīntiān bù néng yóu.
I can swim, but I can't today.

ASGQJ5IC.explain: 还是 offers a choice in a question; 或者 gives alternatives in a statement.
examples: Wǒ hē chá huòzhě kāfēi dōu xíng.
Tea or coffee, either is fine.

ASGPINA4.explain: 别人 means "other people"; 人家 can mean "others", a specific "they", or coyly "me".

ASGN6O6J.explain: 之间 is "between" (two things, people, times); 中间 is "in the middle" of a space.
examples: There are no secrets between us.
liǎng diǎn dào sān diǎn zhījiān

ASG59C66.explain: 离 measures distance between two places; 从 is the starting point of a movement or period.
examples: Wǒ jiā lí gōngsī hěn jìn.
My home is close to the office.
Wǒ cóng jiā zǒu dào gōngsī.
I walk from home to the office.
从这儿到那儿要十分钟。
Cóng zhèr dào nàr yào shí fēnzhōng.
It takes ten minutes from here to there.

ASGLNKZR.explain: 以后 means after an event has finished; 的时候 means during it.
examples: After eating we'll go for a walk.
Chīfàn de shíhou bié kàn shǒujī.
Don't look at your phone while eating.
Xiàkè yǐhòu gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.

ASGB8BWA.explain: 得不得了 after an adjective means "terribly, extremely".

ASGG1ZBL.explain: 得很 after an adjective means "very", stronger than 很 before it.

ASGEHTV5.explain: 有点儿太…了 means "a bit too …".
examples: This is a bit too expensive.
Nǐ shuō de yǒudiǎnr tài kuài le.
You speak a bit too fast.
The room is a bit too small.

ASGQFW44.explain: 都 also means "already" before a time (都十点了), "even" with 连, and "every" with question words.
examples: Dōu shí diǎn le, kuài zǒu ba.

ASG4807F.explain: 还 has many shades: still, even more (比…还), fairly (还可以), and "also, what's more".

examples: The problem will get solved eventually.
Nǐ zǒng děi chī diǎnr dōngxi.
You've got to eat something at least.

ASGJPQ0Q.explain: 看来 means "it seems, it looks like" from what you see.
examples: Kànlái tā bú huì lái le.
It looks like he won't come.

ASG767A2.explain: 只好 means "have no choice but to".
examples: There was no bus, so I had to walk.
Tā bìng le, wǒmen zhǐhǎo gǎitiān.
He's ill, so we'll have to pick another day.
Piào màiwán le, zhǐhǎo bú qù le.
Tickets sold out; nothing for it but not to go.

ASGSPAKW.explain: 可 before an adjective or verb adds emphasis, in speech: "really".

ASG4V36Q.explain: 毕竟 means "after all", giving the basic reason.

ASG78FDE.explain: 再不…就… warns: "if you don't … now, then …".
examples: Zài bù zǒu jiù wǎn le.
If we don't leave now we'll be late.
Zài bù chī jiù liáng le.
Eat now or it'll get cold.
Zài bù xuéxí jiù kǎo bu guò le.
Study now or you won't pass.

ASGGOUJB.explain: 差点儿没 with a wanted result means "almost didn't manage"; with an unwanted one it still means "almost (happened)".

ASGZVM27.explain: 反正 means "anyway, in any case".

ASGINBWJ.explain: 尽量 means "as much as possible, do one's best to".
examples: Drink as much water as you can.
I'm afraid it's going to rain.

ASG81QV3.explain: 好容易 and 好不容易 both mean "with great difficulty, finally".
examples: Wǒ hǎobù róngyì cái zhǎodào nǐ.
I finally found you after a lot of trouble.
It was hard, but I got tickets.
他好不容易考上了大学。
Tā hǎobù róngyì kǎoshàng le dàxué.
He got into university after much effort.

ASGKWV6F.explain: 甚至 means "even", introducing an extreme example.
examples: 他甚至不会写自己的名字。
Tā shènzhì bú huì xiě zìjǐ de míngzi.
He can't even write his own name.
我忙得甚至没时间吃饭。
Wǒ máng de shènzhì méi shíjiān chīfàn.
I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat.

ASG626D3.explain: 尽管 before a verb means "feel free to, go ahead and".
examples: Feel free to ask if you have questions.

ASG0C825.explain: 不得不 means "have no choice but to".
examples: We had no choice but to change the plan.

ASGTVEHJ.explain: 到底 in a question presses for the answer: "what on earth, after all".
examples: What on earth is going on?

ASGDK0BR.explain: 究竟 is like 到底 but more formal: "exactly, after all".

ASGZ8MJM.explain: 干脆 means "might as well, simply".

examples: Wǒ jīhū měi tiān dōu qù.
Wǒ zài yě bú qù le.
Tā zài yě bù hējiǔ le.
Wǒ zài yě bù xiāngxìn tā le.

ASG16EF6.explain: 曾经 means "once, formerly", often with 过.

ASG6F157.explain: 本来 means "originally", often for a plan that changed.
examples: It was never easy in the first place.

ASGP6LVA.explain: 再三 means "over and over, repeatedly".
examples: He thanked me again and again.
I thought it over many times.

ASGACMNQ.explain: 一向 means "always, all along" (a habit up to now).

ASGIVGZO.pattern: 千万 + 别 / 要 + verb
ASGIVGZO.explain: 千万 strengthens a warning: "be sure to, whatever you do".

ASGTIMTS.explain: 白 before a verb means "in vain, for nothing".
examples: Wǒ bái děng le yí ge xiǎoshí.
I waited an hour for nothing.

ASG5334C.explain: 顺便 means "while you're at it, in passing".
examples: Grab a bottle of water while you're at it.
By the way, let me ask.
Huí jiā shí shùnbiàn kànkan tā.
Drop in on him on your way home.

ASGF08B6.explain: 又 marks an action repeated in the past.
examples: Wǒ yòu kàn le yí biàn.

ASGMCP9V.explain: 难道 makes a rhetorical question: "could it really be that …?", "don't tell me …".
examples: Don't tell me you don't know?

ASGQAN74.explain: 差很多 and 差得远 mean "very different, far off", the opposite of 差不多.
examples: Zhè liǎng ge chà hěn duō.
Wǒ de Zhōngwén gēn tā chà de yuǎn.
My Chinese is far behind his.

ASGGPG97.explain: 啊 after each item lists things casually.
examples: 苹果啊，香蕉啊，我都喜欢。
Píngguǒ a, xiāngjiāo a, wǒ dōu xǐhuan.
Apples, bananas… I like them all.
Chànggē a, tiàowǔ a, tā dōu huì.
Singing, dancing… he can do it all.
Běijīng a, Shànghǎi a, dōu qùguo.
Beijing, Shanghai… been to them all.
下雨了，于是我们回家了。
Xià yǔ le, yúshì wǒmen huí jiā le.
It started raining, so we went home.
他没来，于是会议取消了。
Tā méi lái, yúshì huìyì qǔxiāo le.
He didn't come, so the meeting was cancelled.
Wǒ è le, yúshì qù chīfàn.
I was hungry, and so I went to eat.

ASGMX0ZS.explain: 而 joins two contrasting clauses: "while, whereas".
examples: 他喜欢茶，而我喜欢咖啡。
Tā xǐhuan chá, ér wǒ xǐhuan kāfēi.
He likes tea, whereas I like coffee.
This is expensive but not good.
我们不是为了钱，而是为了朋友。
Wǒmen bú shì wèile qián, ér shì wèile péngyou.
We're not doing it for money but for a friend.

ASGS4DBY.explain: 当中 means "among, in the middle of".
examples: 在学生当中他很受欢迎。
Zài xuésheng dāngzhōng tā hěn shòu huānyíng.
这些书当中我最喜欢这本。
Zhèxiē shū dāngzhōng wǒ zuì xǐhuan zhè běn.
Of these books I like this one best.

ASGF205D.explain: 彼此 means "each other", a bit more formal than 互相.

ASG75EE1.explain: 当…的时候 means "when …", slightly formal.
examples: 当我到家的时候，他已经走了。
Dāng wǒ dào jiā de shíhou, tā yǐjīng zǒu le.
When I got home he had already left.
当你有空的时候，给我打电话。
Dāng nǐ yǒu kòng de shíhou, gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.

ASGD1LNT.explain: 其中 means "among them, of which".
examples: 我有三本书，其中一本是中文的。
Wǒ yǒu sān běn shū, qízhōng yì běn shì Zhōngwén de.
I have three books, one of which is in Chinese.
来了十个人，其中五个是学生。
Lái le shí ge rén, qízhōng wǔ ge shì xuésheng.
Ten people came, five of them students.
The reasons behind it are complicated.

ASGNPO4V.explain: 这个 between a pronoun and a noun makes name-calling: 你这个笨蛋.

ASG4K5WH.explain: With a bare object, 了 goes at the end; with a counted object, after the verb. Both can appear together.
examples: Wǒ chī le liǎng wǎn fàn.
I ate two bowls of rice.
Wǒ yǐjīng chī le fàn le.

ASG890CA.explain: With a result or direction complement, 了 goes after the complement.

ASGB33AE.explain: 嘛 after a topic pauses on it: "as for …".
examples: Zhè jiàn shì ma, yǐhòu zài shuō.
As for this, let's talk later.

ASGW7YXP.explain: 呢 at the end of a question word question softens the tone.
examples: Where are you off to, then?

ASG7AE5C.pattern: 最多 / 至少 / 最少 + number
ASG7AE5C.explain: 最多 at most; 至少 or 最少 at least.
examples: It costs at least a hundred yuan.
Zhìshǎo lái le èrshí ge rén.
Suízhe shíjiān guòqù, tā wàng le.
随着经济发展，生活好了。
Suízhe jīngjì fāzhǎn, shēnghuó hǎo le.
With economic growth, life has improved.
自从来中国，我每天说中文。
Zìcóng lái Zhōngguó, wǒ měi tiān shuō Zhōngwén.
Since coming to China I speak Chinese daily.
Zìcóng qùnián, tā méi huíguo jiā.
He hasn't been home since last year.

ASGD2A08.explain: 对…而言 is a formal "for, as far as … is concerned".
examples: Duì wǒ éryán, zhè hěn zhòngyào.
Duì háizi éryán tài nán le.
包括我在内，一共五个人。
Bāokuò wǒ zàinèi, yígòng wǔ ge rén.
Including me, five people in all.
Lián tā zàinèi dōu bù zhīdào.

ASGGB3IV.explain: 凭 means "on the basis of, relying on".

ASGEZ2HN.pattern: subject + 给 + doer + verb + 了
ASGEZ2HN.explain: In speech, 给 can make a passive like 被, usually for something that went wrong.
examples: Wǒ de shū gěi tā názǒu le.
My book was taken away by him.

ASGZRKTG.explain: 至于 switches to another topic: "as for".
examples: As for the price, we'll talk later.
As for him, I'm not sure.
至于什么时候去，还没定。
Zhìyú shénme shíhou qù, hái méi dìng.
As for when to go, it's not decided.

ASG8RW47.explain: 就…来说 limits the scope: "as far as … goes".
examples: As far as I'm concerned, no problem.
as far as this matter goes
Chèn tā bú zài, wǒmen zǒu ba.

ASGUQUPG.explain: 并 before a negation stresses it against an expectation: "not at all, actually not".

ASG8F7D4.explain: 要不是 means "if it weren't for".
examples: Yàobúshì nǐ, wǒ jiù chídào le.
If it weren't for you, I'd have been late.
要不是下雨，我们就去了。
Yàobúshì xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù qù le.
If it hadn't rained, we'd have gone.

ASG6TB4J.explain: 而已 at the end means "that's all, merely".
examples: I was just asking, that's all.

ASG68DA5.explain: 将 is the formal, written equivalent of 把.
examples: Tā jiāng shū fàng zài zhuō shang.
He put the book on the table.

ASGN3IGH.explain: 什么 after a verb challenges it: "what are you … for?".

examples: Tā chàng de xiàng gēshǒu yíyàng hǎo.
She sings as well as a singer.
Today is as hot as summer.
Compared with Beijing, Shanghai is hotter.
Bǐqǐ yǐqián, tā shòu duō le.
Compared with before, he's much thinner.
比起开车，我更喜欢走路。
Bǐqǐ kāichē, wǒ gèng xǐhuan zǒulù.

ASGWH1D5.explain: 不如 means "not as good as"; alone it suggests "might as well".
examples: I'm not as good as him.
This isn't as good as that.

ASGS6UKN.explain: 化 makes "-ize" words: 现代化 modernise, 简化 simplify.

ASGYKH5G.explain: 难怪 as a verb means "no wonder" or "can't blame".
examples: No wonder you don't get it.

ASGIQPUJ.explain: 将 before a verb is a formal "will".
examples: The meeting will be held tomorrow.
他同意并支持这个计划。
Tā tóngyì bìng zhīchí zhège jìhuà.
He agrees with and supports the plan.

ASGGNXVR.explain: 由 names who does something, formally: "by".
examples: Zhè jiàn shì yóu wǒ fùzé.
The costs are paid by the company.

ASGYDKT3.explain: 难免 means "hard to avoid, inevitable".
examples: It's natural to be nervous at first.
He's clever and works hard too.
It's cheap, and good quality as well.
It's not worth getting angry about.
Tā hài de wǒ chídào le.
It made everyone wait for nothing.
It cost me a good night's sleep.

ASG1DXUD.explain: 受 makes a passive with nouns: 受欢迎 popular, 受伤 get hurt, 受影响 affected.

ASG7AUNJ.explain: Doubling verb + 着 means "kept on …ing (and then)".
examples: He talked and talked, then burst into tears.
Wǒ zǒuzhe zǒuzhe jiù mílù le.
I walked on and on and got lost.
She read and read until she fell asleep.

ASGW863F.explain: 尽管 as a conjunction means "although, even though".
examples: 尽管很难，我还是做完了。
Jǐnguǎn hěn nán, wǒ háishi zuòwán le.
Even though it was hard, I finished it.
Jǐnguǎn xià yǔ, tā háishi lái le.
Although it rained, he still came.

ASG1RE80.explain: 倒 (dào) marks something contrary to expectation: "actually, on the contrary".
examples: I actually don't think it's expensive.
He, on the contrary, is happy.

ASGX5QTV.explain: 反而 means "on the contrary, instead".
examples: Chī le yào, fǎn'ér gèng nánshòu le.
After taking the medicine I felt even worse.
他不但不生气，反而笑了。
Tā búdàn bù shēngqì, fǎn'ér xiào le.
Far from being angry, he laughed.
The more you hurry, the slower it goes.

ASGEG2QB.explain: 却 is "however, but" placed after the subject.
examples: Wǒ xiǎng qù, tā què bù xiǎng.
I want to go, but he doesn't.
天气很冷，他却只穿了一件衬衫。
Tiānqì hěn lěng, tā què zhǐ chuān le yí jiàn chènshān.
It's cold, yet he's only wearing a shirt.
Tā hěn nǔlì, què méi chénggōng.
He worked hard but didn't succeed.

ASGL90MR.explain: 由于 means "due to, owing to", formal.
examples: Yóuyú xià yǔ, bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
Due to rain, the match was cancelled.
由于时间关系，我们先到这儿。
Yóuyú shíjiān guānxi, wǒmen xiān dào zhèr.
Because of time, we'll stop here.

ASGG4BX9.explain: 既然 means "since / given that", drawing a conclusion from a known fact.
examples: 既然你不想去，就别去了。
Jìrán nǐ bù xiǎng qù, jiù bié qù le.
Since you don't want to go, don't.
既然来了，就多住几天吧。
Jìrán lái le, jiù duō zhù jǐ tiān ba.
Since you're here, stay a few more days.
既然大家都同意，就这样决定。
Jìrán dàjiā dōu tóngyì, jiù zhèyàng juédìng.
Tā bìng le, yīncǐ méi lái.
He was ill and therefore didn't come.
价格太高，因此卖不出去。
Jiàgé tài gāo, yīncǐ mài bu chūqù.
The price is too high, so it won't sell.

ASGTPGXK.explain: The effect can come first, then 是因为 gives the cause.
examples: Wǒ méi qù, shì yīnwèi xià yǔ.
I didn't go because it rained.
He was late because of traffic.
Wǒ xué Zhōngwén shì yīnwèi xǐhuan.
I study Chinese because I like it.

ASG9E5BB.explain: After 得, a whole clause can describe the result: so … that.
examples: Tā lèi de zhàn bu qǐlái.
He's so tired he can't stand up.
Tā xiào de yǎnlèi dōu chūlái le.
Wǒ máng de wàng le chīfàn.
I was so busy I forgot to eat.

ASG516F9.pattern: verb + 得 / 不 + 了 (liǎo) / 动 / 起
ASG516F9.explain: More potential complements: 吃不了 can't eat (that much), 走不动 can't walk (no strength), 买不起 can't afford.
examples: Wǒ chī bu liǎo zhème duō.
Tài guì le, mǎi bu qǐ.
Too expensive; I can't afford it.

ASG4OM4T.pattern: verb + 住 / 开 / 出来
ASG4OM4T.explain: More result complements: 住 hold firmly, 开 open/apart, 出来 come out / figure out.
examples: Wǒ tīng chūlái le, shì nǐ.
I could tell by the voice: it's you.

ASGSCN01.pattern: verb + 起来 (begin · put away · seem)
ASGSCN01.explain: 起来 also means to start (哭起来), to gather or put away (收起来), and to judge by (说起来).
examples: Shuō qǐlái róngyì, zuò qǐlái nán.

ASGT0GYL.explain: 坏了 after a verb means "broken" or, with feelings, "extremely".

ASGM5ZAB.explain: 着, read zháo here, means the action reached its goal: 睡着 fall asleep, 找着 find, 买着 manage to buy.
examples: Did you manage to get tickets?

ASGCUSIV.pattern: verb + 到 (reach · until · to the point)
ASGCUSIV.explain: 到 after a verb can mean reaching a goal (买到), a time (等到五点), or a degree (想不到).
examples: I didn't expect you to come.

ASGYJQAG.explain: V来V去 means doing something back and forth, around.
examples: Wǒ xiǎng lái xiǎng qù, háishi bú qù.
After thinking it over and over, I'm still not going.
Shuō lái shuō qù dōu shì yíyàng de.
However you put it, it's the same.

ASG98C1A.explain: 只要…就… means "as long as …, then …": a sufficient condition.
examples: As long as you work hard, you can learn it well.
Zhǐyào nǐ lái, wǒ jiù gāoxìng.
As long as you come, I'm happy.
Zhǐyào bú xià yǔ jiù qù.
We'll go as long as it doesn't rain.
Yídàn kāishǐ, jiù bù néng tíng.
Once you start, you can't stop.
一旦有消息，我就告诉你。
Yídàn yǒu xiāoxi, wǒ jiù gàosu nǐ.
As soon as there's news I'll tell you.

ASG9E9A6.explain: 才 after a condition means "only then, not until".
examples: Chī le yào cái huì hǎo.
You'll only get better once you take the medicine.
Tā lái le wǒ cái zǒu.
I'll leave only when he comes.
Only after homework can you play.

ASGJDV3Y.explain: 只有…才… means "only if …, (only then) …": one necessary condition.
examples: Only by working hard can you succeed.
Zhǐyǒu duō tīng, cái néng tīngdǒng.
Only by listening a lot can you understand.
Chúfēi nǐ qù, wǒ cái qù.
I'll go only if you go.
Chúfēi xià yǔ, fǒuzé wǒmen qù.
Jíshǐ xià yǔ, wǒ yě qù.
Even if it rains, I'll go.
Jíshǐ hěn nán, yě yào shì yi shì.
Even if it's hard, give it a try.
即使他不来，我们也开始。
Jíshǐ tā bù lái, wǒmen yě kāishǐ.
Even if he doesn't come, we'll start.

ASGF1TQ2.explain: 就是…也… is a spoken "even if".
examples: Jiùshì xià yǔ, wǒ yě qù.
Even if it rains, I'll go.
Jiùshì bú shuìjiào, yě yào zuòwán.
Even without sleep, I'll finish it.
Jiùshì tā lái, wǒ yě bú pà.
Even if he comes, I'm not afraid.
Jiùsuàn hěn nán, yě yào shìshi.
Even if it's hard, give it a try.
Jiùsuàn nǐ bù shuō, wǒ yě zhīdào.
Even if you don't say it, I know.
Jiùsuàn yǒu qián, yě bù mǎi.
Even with money, I wouldn't buy it.

ASGXX3NY.explain: 哪怕 means "even if, no matter how".
examples: 哪怕只有一分钟，也要见你。
Nǎpà zhǐ yǒu yì fēnzhōng, yě yào jiàn nǐ.
Even if only for a minute, I want to see you.
Nǎpà zài máng, yě yào chīfàn.
Even if I fail, I won't regret it.

ASGHNDX4.explain: 假如 means "if, supposing", a little more formal than 如果.
examples: Jiǎrú wǒ shì nǐ, wǒ jiù qù.
If I were you, I'd go.
Jiǎrú yǒu shíjiān, wǒ huì lái.
If I have time, I'll come.
Yàoshi nǐ bù lái, wǒ jiù zǒu.
If you don't come, I'll leave.
Yàoshi yǒu qián jiù hǎo le.

ASG25773.explain: 万一 means "what if, in case" (something unlikely and bad).
examples: Bring an umbrella in case it rains.
万一他不来，我们怎么办？
Wànyī tā bù lái, wǒmen zěnme bàn?

ASGB0MXK.explain: 的话 can mark a topic: "as for …, if it's …".
examples: If it's you, I believe it.

ASG0NDS6.explain: 不管…都… is the spoken version of 无论: "no matter …".
examples: Bùguǎn nǐ qù bu qù, wǒ dōu qù.
Whether you go or not, I'm going.
不管什么时候，你都可以来。
Bùguǎn shénme shíhou, nǐ dōu kěyǐ lái.
Bùguǎn duō guì, tā dōu mǎi.

ASG6ZI8L.explain: 无论…都… means "no matter …". The first part holds a question word or a choice.
examples: 无论多忙，他都坚持锻炼。
Wúlùn duō máng, tā dōu jiānchí duànliàn.
No matter how busy, he keeps exercising.
无论你去哪儿，我都跟你去。
Wúlùn nǐ qù nǎr, wǒ dōu gēn nǐ qù.
Wherever you go, I'll go with you.
Wúlùn guì bu guì, wǒ dōu yào mǎi.
Expensive or not, I'm buying it.

ASGQRS3P.pattern: 把 + object + verb + 成 / 给 / 在
ASGQRS3P.explain: 把 with 成 (turn into), 给 (hand to) or 在 (put at) describes what happened to the object.
examples: He treats me as a friend.
Park the car at the door.

ASGF273F.pattern: 连 + verb + 都 + 不 / 没
ASGF273F.explain: 连 can stress a verb too: "didn't even …".
examples: Tā lián kàn dōu méi kàn.
Wǒ lián xiǎng dōu bù gǎn xiǎng.
I don't even dare think about it.

ASG8DVSO.explain: 不比 means "not more … than" (they may be equal).
examples: Today is no colder than yesterday.

ASGXGADL.explain: 要 at the start of a clause can mean "if", with 就 for the result.
examples: Yào xià yǔ, jiù bié qù le.
Yào bù xiǎng qù, jiù shuō.
If you don't want to go, say so.
Nǐ yào lèi le, jiù xiūxi.

ASGP8DXU.explain: 任何 means "any", usually with 都.

examples: It's both quiet and convenient here.
jì shěng qián yòu shěng shíjiān

ASG3IR71.explain: 少不了 means "can't do without, bound to have".
examples: New Year isn't complete without dumplings.
We can't do this without you.
This amounts to doing it for nothing.

ASGEB7F5.explain: 从…中 means "from (within)", for abstract sources.

ASGL4O5E.explain: Repeating a verb around 就 shows indifference: "so be it".
examples: Tā bù lái jiù bù lái.
If he won't come, so be it.

ASGBA782.explain: 无…可… means "nothing to …": 无话可说 nothing to say.

ASGUQ861.pattern: 一 + measure word + 都 / 也 + 不 / 没
ASGUQ861.explain: 一 + measure word with 都不 means "not even one".
examples: Yí ge rén dōu méi lái.
Wǒ yí jù huà yě méi shuō.

ASGF9320.explain: 不但…甚至连…都… means "not only …, even …".
examples: 他不但会中文，甚至连方言都会。
Tā búdàn huì Zhōngwén, shènzhì lián fāngyán dōu huì.
He not only speaks Chinese, he even speaks dialects.
不但大人，甚至连孩子都知道。
Búdàn dàrén, shènzhì lián háizi dōu zhīdào.
Not only adults, even children know.
不但没帮忙，甚至连话都不说。
Búdàn méi bāngmáng, shènzhì lián huà dōu bù shuō.
Not only didn't he help, he didn't even speak.

ASG18JOA.explain: 好 can introduce a purpose: "so that".
examples: Zǎo diǎn shuì, hǎo míngtiān zǎo qǐ.
Go to bed early so you can get up early tomorrow.
Duō dài diǎnr qián, hǎo mǎi dōngxi.
Bring more money so you can shop.
Tell me so I can prepare.
It has to do with the weather.

ASG1QB4K.explain: 一面…一面… is like 一边…一边…, a little more formal.
examples: work and study at the same time
What we call success is persistence.

ASGB44F6.explain: 越…越… means "the more …, the more …".
examples: The rain is getting heavier and heavier.
The more I think about it, the angrier I get.

ASGEXR6R.explain: 不是…就是… means "if not …, then …": only two possibilities.
examples: 他不是在家，就是在公司。
Tā bú shì zài jiā, jiùshì zài gōngsī.
He's either at home or at the office.
我宁可走路，也不坐他的车。
Wǒ nìngkě zǒulù, yě bú zuò tā de chē.
I'd rather walk than ride in his car.
他宁可不吃饭，也要把工作做完。
Tā nìngkě bù chīfàn, yě yào bǎ gōngzuò zuòwán.
He'd rather skip dinner than leave the work unfinished.
宁可慢一点儿，也别出错。
Nìngkě màn yìdiǎnr, yě bié chūcuò.
Better to be a bit slow than make mistakes.

ASGYXI5X.explain: 或者…或者… means "either … or …" in statements.
examples: Huòzhě nǐ lái, huòzhě wǒ qù.
Either you come or I go.
Either by bus or on foot.
我连走路都累，别说跑步了。
Wǒ lián zǒulù dōu lèi, bié shuō pǎobù le.
Even walking tires me, let alone running.
Tā bú huì dú, bié shuō xiě le.
He can't read it, let alone write it.
一块钱都没有，别说一百了。
Yí kuài qián dōu méiyǒu, bié shuō yìbǎi le.
Not even one yuan, let alone a hundred.

ASGHOI8S.explain: 更不用说 means "not to mention, let alone".
examples: 我没时间睡觉，更不用说玩了。
Wǒ méi shíjiān shuìjiào, gèng búyòng shuō wán le.
I've no time to sleep, let alone play.
孩子都懂，更不用说大人了。
Háizi dōu dǒng, gèng búyòng shuō dàrén le.
Even children get it, not to mention adults.
北京都没去过，更不用说上海了。
Běijīng dōu méi qùguo, gèng búyòng shuō Shànghǎi le.
Never been to Beijing, let alone Shanghai.

ASGJ1VZQ.pattern: 不仅 / 不光 / 不只 …，也 / 还 / 而且 …
ASGJ1VZQ.explain: 不但, 不仅, 不光 and 不只 all mean "not only", paired with 而且, 也 or 还.
examples: 他不仅会唱歌，还会跳舞。
Tā bùjǐn huì chànggē, hái huì tiàowǔ.
He not only sings but also dances.
Not just me, everyone is going.
Not only cheap but also handy.

ASG56QKW.explain: Both mean "originally"; only 原来 also means "it turns out that".

ASGLOS9C.explain: 就 = sooner, easier or less than expected; 才 = later, harder or more than expected. Both go before the verb; 就 often takes 了, 才 doesn't.
examples: Tā bā diǎn jiù lái le.
He came as early as eight.
我看了一遍就懂了，他看了三遍才懂。
Wǒ kàn le yí biàn jiù dǒng le, tā kàn le sān biàn cái dǒng.
I understood after one reading; he needed three.

ASGE09B4.explain: 常常 is "often" for anything; 往往 is "tends to", a pattern under certain conditions, not for the future.
examples: He tends to be busy at weekends.
Tiān lěng de shíhou wǎngwǎng xià xuě.
When it's cold it often snows.

ASGTBHBG.explain: 再 is "again" for the future; 又 for something that already happened again.

ASGT8AUA.explain: Both mean "finally"; 总算 adds relief ("at last, phew"), 终于 is neutral.

ASGC5Y86.explain: 跟 is "with" (together, or the other side of an exchange); 对 is "to, towards" (one direction).

ASGIHS2L.explain: All mean "towards": 往 for movement (往前走), 向 for movement and abstract direction (向他学习), 朝 for facing (朝南).

ASG3JELV.explain: 对于 is a formal "regarding" for topics; 对 also works with people and actions.
examples: 对于这个问题，我没意见。
Duìyú zhège wèntí, wǒ méi yìjiàn.
Regarding this question, I have no objection.

ASGC01S0.explain: 对于 means "regarding" a topic; 至于 changes to a new topic, "as for".
examples: Duìyú zhè jiàn shì, wǒ hěn bàoqiàn.
至于他去不去，我不知道。
Zhìyú tā qù bu qù, wǒ bù zhīdào.
As for whether he goes, I don't know.

ASG863DE.explain: 给 is "for/to" someone in everyday speech; 为 is "for the sake of", more formal.

ASG1HNBU.explain: 关于 is "about" (the content); 对于 is "regarding" (the attitude or treatment).
examples: As to this plan, I agree.

ASGVDOXL.explain: 适合 is a verb ("suits", takes an object); 合适 is an adjective ("suitable").

ASGJOGGG.explain: 平时 is a noun, "usually, in normal times"; 平常 is also an adjective, "ordinary".
examples: I usually get up at seven.

ASGC3SCN.explain: Both mean "after"; 之后 is a bit more formal and always follows something, while 以后 can stand alone ("in the future").

ASGNPJ7T.pattern: 以后 · 然后 · 后来
ASGNPJ7T.explain: 以后 = after (any time); 然后 = and then (next step); 后来 = later on (past narration).
examples: Eat first, then watch a film.

ASG54932.explain: 看起来 describes appearance ("looks"); 看来 draws a conclusion ("it seems that").
examples: Kànlái tā bú huì lái le.

ASGKQEG9.explain: 显得 means "appears (to be)", often because of something; 看起来 is "looks" from a glance.

ASGXXP6M.explain: 倒 / 倒是 can concede, urge or soften: "well, actually".
examples: This method is actually not bad.
我倒是想去，可惜没时间。
Wǒ dàoshì xiǎng qù, kěxī méi shíjiān.
I'd like to go, but sadly there's no time.

ASGA1B87.explain: 很是 is a formal, emphatic "very".

ASGJIFI9.explain: 足足 means "a full, no less than".
examples: Wǒ děng le zúzú liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
I waited a full two hours.
Tā zúzú gāo le shí límǐ.
He grew a full ten centimetres.
no fewer than a hundred people

ASG47D26.explain: 一再 means "again and again, repeatedly".

examples: Fánshì lái de rén dōu yǒu lǐwù.
Everyone who comes gets a gift.
Fánshì tā shuō de, wǒ dōu xìn.

ASGDU0XL.explain: 向来 means "always, all along" up to now.

ASGC11D0.explain: 果然 means "as expected, sure enough".

ASGB316B.explain: 似乎 means "it seems, as if", formal.

ASGFZOLQ.explain: 偏偏 means "contrary to what one would want, of all things".
examples: Wǒ yào chūmén, piānpiān xià yǔ le.
Just as I was leaving, it had to rain.
Of all days, today I didn't bring money.

ASGAA381.explain: 再不…也… means "even if not …, still …" (concession).
examples: Zài bù hǎochī, yě yào chīwán.
However bad it tastes, finish it.
Zài bú yuànyì, yě děi qù.
However unwilling, you have to go.
Zài bù gāoxìng yě bié fāhuǒ.
However upset, don't lose your temper.

ASGC8A38.explain: 一律 means "without exception, all alike".
examples: No one is allowed in, no exceptions.

ASG0D90L.explain: 竟然 means "unexpectedly, actually" with surprise.

ASGMDJTD.explain: 到时候 means "when the time comes".
examples: We'll see when the time comes.
Dào shíhou wǒ gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
I'll call you when it's time.
Dào shíhou nǐ jiù míngbai le.
You'll understand when the time comes.

ASG3AD49.explain: 何必 means "why bother / there's no need to", a rhetorical question.
examples: No need to be so polite.

ASGPV5Z2.explain: 来着 at the end of a question asks about something you knew but forgot: "what was it again?".
examples: What did you just say again?
Where did we go yesterday, again?

ASGCC713.explain: 以及 means "as well as", formal, usually before the last item.
examples: 老师、学生以及家长都来了。
Lǎoshī, xuésheng yǐjí jiāzhǎng dōu lái le.
Teachers, students and parents all came.

ASGF561D.explain: 总之 means "in short, in a word".

ASG3GX2H.explain: 则 is a written "whereas, on the other hand".
examples: Nánfāng duō yǔ, běifāng zé gānzào.
The south is rainy, whereas the north is dry.
他喜欢茶，我则喜欢咖啡。
Tā xǐhuan chá, wǒ zé xǐhuan kāfēi.
He likes tea; I, on the other hand, like coffee.

ASG0A67E.explain: 以免 means "so as to avoid, lest".
examples: Leave early so as not to be late.
Wear more to avoid catching a cold.
Keep quiet so as not to disturb others.

ASGH4A7W.explain: 本 before a noun means "this, our": 本人 I myself, 本公司 our company.

ASGDZIO0.explain: 性 makes abstract nouns: 重要性 importance, 可能性 possibility.

ASGNLGGX.explain: 是否 is a formal "whether or not".
examples: I don't know whether he agrees.
May I ask whether you're free?
Whether it's correct is still unclear.

ASGBAIMA.explain: 之 is a written, classical "of": in fractions and percentages (三分之一), and in set phrases (之前, 之后, 之一).
examples: 他是我最好的朋友之一。
Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou zhī yī.
He is one of my best friends.

ASGTVKAR.explain: 与否 after a verb or adjective means "or not", formal.
examples: Whether it succeeds or not isn't important.
Please reply whether you agree or not.

ASGVBH2H.explain: In written Chinese 被 also works as a prefix meaning "being made to": 被动 passive, 被告 the accused.

ASGC1BI5.explain: 鉴于 means "in view of, considering", formal.
examples: In view of the weather, the match is postponed.
in light of the above reasons
鉴于他的表现，我们录用他。
Jiànyú tā de biǎoxiàn, wǒmen lùyòng tā.
Given his performance, we're hiring him.

ASG50DR1.explain: 非…不可 means "must, absolutely have to".
examples: I simply have to buy this.

ASG5HZG6.explain: 岂不是 is a formal rhetorical "wouldn't that be …?".
examples: Zhèyàng qǐ bú shì gèng hǎo?
Isn't that a waste of time?
Nǐ qǐ bú shì bái lái le?
Then didn't you come for nothing?

ASGKU8FU.explain: 兼 means "concurrently, at the same time" for roles.
examples: He's a teacher and a writer.

ASGYYOXD.explain: 莫非 means "could it be that …?".
examples: Is it possible you don't know?
From this we can see he works hard.

ASGK0ZG7.explain: 非得 means "must, have to", colloquial.
examples: Do you really have to go today?
He insists on doing it himself.
It has to be said now.

ASGGI66V.explain: 莫过于 means "nothing is more … than".
examples: 最幸福的事莫过于回家。
Zuì xìngfú de shì mòguòyú huí jiā.
Nothing is happier than going home.
最好的礼物莫过于时间。
Zuì hǎo de lǐwù mòguòyú shíjiān.

ASGWI5CV.explain: 与其…不如… means "rather than …, better to …".
examples: Rather than wait, better to go.
Better to change than to complain.
Rather than buy it, borrow it.

ASGA77KW.explain: 跟…似的 or 像…似的 means "as if, like".

ASGMCX2H.explain: 不愧是 means "truly deserves to be called, worthy of".
examples: He's a champion and no mistake.
Peking duck lives up to its name.

ASGU98B7.explain: 由…做主 means "it's up to … to decide".
examples: Zhè jiàn shì yóu nǐ zuòzhǔ.
This is for you to decide.
At home, mum has the say.

ASGK4CGK.explain: 一来…二来… lists reasons: "firstly …, secondly …".
examples: Yīlái tài guì, èrlái méi yòng.
Yīlái shěng qián, èrlái shěng shíjiān.
For one it saves money, for another, time.
一来我忙，二来我不想去。
Yīlái wǒ máng, èrlái wǒ bù xiǎng qù.
For one thing I'm busy; for another I don't want to go.

ASGWSSQL.explain: 以…为… means "take A as B": 以…为主 mainly, 以…为例 for example.

ASGOR3M4.pattern: 谅 + person + 不敢 / 不会 …
ASGOR3M4.explain: 谅 here means "I bet (he wouldn't dare)".
examples: I bet he won't dare come.
Liàng nǐ yě bú huì shuō.
Liàng tā bù gǎn piàn wǒ.
I bet he wouldn't dare lie to me.

ASGA632B.explain: 在于 means "lies in, depends on".

ASGE2U25.explain: 不屑 means "disdain to, think it beneath one".
examples: She wouldn't lower herself to talk to him.

ASGXU2H4.explain: 以便 means "so as to, in order to" (make easier).
examples: Please leave a number so we can contact you.
早点准备，以便按时完成。
Zǎo diǎn zhǔnbèi, yǐbiàn ànshí wánchéng.
Prepare early so as to finish on time.
He was absent because of illness.
假使他不来，我们就开始。
Jiǎshǐ tā bù lái, wǒmen jiù kāishǐ.
If he doesn't come, we'll start.
Jiǎshǐ yǒu wèntí, qǐng gàosu wǒ.
Should there be a problem, tell me.

ASG6509E.explain: 为…而… means "do … for the sake of …".

ASG9D48A.explain: 以…的名义 means "in the name of".
examples: yǐ péngyou de míngyì bāng tā

ASG3ZS9G.explain: 何况 means "let alone, much less" or "besides".
examples: 大人都搬不动，何况孩子。
Dàrén dōu bān bu dòng, hékuàng háizi.
Even adults can't lift it, let alone children.
太贵了，何况我也不喜欢。
Tài guì le, hékuàng wǒ yě bù xǐhuan.
Too expensive; besides, I don't like it.

ASGEA938.explain: 按照 is "according to" a rule or plan to follow; 根据 is "based on" evidence or a source.
examples: 根据天气预报，明天下雨。
Gēnjù tiānqì yùbào, míngtiān xià yǔ.
According to the forecast, it'll rain tomorrow.

ASG73H8K.explain: Both mean "have no choice but to"; 不得不 stresses the pressure, 只好 the lack of better options.
examples: No tickets, so we just went home.
He had to admit the mistake.

ASGIKHUH.explain: 不断 means "continuously" over a long time (progress, change); 不停 means "without stopping" for a concrete action.

ASG0K25S.explain: 却 is "but" (contrast); 反而 is "on the contrary" (the opposite of what was expected).
examples: Tā hěn nǔlì, què méi tōngguò.
He worked hard but didn't pass.
Chī le yào fǎn'ér gèng nánshòu.
After the medicine I felt even worse.
Tiānqì lěng, tā què bù chuān wàitào.
It's cold, yet he wears no coat.

ASG9JK0B.explain: 根本 is "at all, fundamentally" (usually in negatives); 到底 is "on earth, after all" in questions, or "finally".
examples: I had no idea at all.
There's no such thing at all.

ASGXJYJD.explain: 据 is a short, written 根据: 据说 it is said, 据我所知 as far as I know.

ASGGXSIR.explain: 恢复 means "recover, restore" (health, order, a function); 还原 means "restore to the original state" (an object, a scene).
examples: Put the room back as it was.

ASGCZ37R.explain: 居然 is "unexpectedly" (surprise); 反而 is "on the contrary" (the opposite result).
examples: Búdàn méi hǎo, fǎn'ér gèng zāo.
Far from better, it got worse.

ASGBVSWQ.explain: 一时 means "for a moment, momentarily"; 一度 means "once, at one time" in the past.
examples: I can't recall it for the moment.

ASGVEP8S.explain: 一直 is "continuously" (an action or state without a break); 一向 is "always" (a habit or character).
examples: He's been working the whole time.

ASG84D65.explain: 彼此 means "each other" (both sides); 对方 means "the other side" (from one side's view).

ASGFNS52.explain: 反而 is an adverb inside a sentence ("instead"); 相反 starts a new sentence ("on the contrary") or is an adjective ("opposite").
examples: Tā méi shēngqì, fǎn'ér xiào le.
He wasn't angry; instead he laughed.
On the contrary, I think it's good.

de-adverbial.title: Adverbs with "de" (地)
de-adverbial.explain: 地 turns an adjective into an adverb that describes the verb after it. Two-syllable or repeated adjectives take 地; compare 得, which comes after the verb.
de-adverbial.note: 地 is read de here; as a noun it is dì (ground).
